title: Apostrophes: Contraction and Possession (KS2)
subject: English
strapline: The two jobs of the apostrophe — and the its/it's trap.
facts: An apostrophe has two jobs: to show missing letters (contraction) or to show belonging (possession).
Contraction: do not → don't, it is → it's, they are → they're. The apostrophe marks where letters were removed.
Singular possession: add 's — "the dog's bowl" means the bowl of one dog.
Plural possession (regular): add just an apostrophe after the s — "the dogs' bowls" means bowls of many dogs.
its (no apostrophe) means belonging to it; it's (with apostrophe) means it is or it has — this is the most common mistake.
Apostrophes are NOT used to make ordinary plurals: it is "apples", not "apple's".
For a name ending in s, you can still add 's: "James's book".

quick_quiz.q: Which is correct: "its raining" or "it's raining"?
How do you show a bowl belonging to one cat?
True or false: you add an apostrophe to make "banana" plural.

teacher_tips: Teach the two jobs separately before mixing them.
Drill its vs it's with the "does it mean it is?" test.
Hunt for "greengrocer's apostrophes" on real signs — memorable and fun.
